title: Infeksi Sistem Saraf Pusat
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_infection
summary: Kuliah komprehensif tentang infeksi SSP yang mencakup meningitis, ensefalitis, abses otak, dan mielitis. Menyajikan pendekatan diagnosis dengan lumbal pungsi, analisis LCS, temuan pencitraan, serta protokol terapi spesifik untuk toksoplasmosis, meningitis TB, meningitis kriptokokus, meningitis bakterialis, ensefalitis viral, dan abses otak. Menekankan prinsip lokalisasi infeksi, penentuan etiologi, dan terapi yang sesuai dengan lokasi.

sections.title: Prinsip Pendekatan Penyakit Infeksi

content.text: The approach to CNS infections is guided by two fundamental questions: Where is the infection located? And what is the causative organism? Therapy must reach the infection site and must be appropriate to the specific pathogen identified or suspected.

sections.title: Tersangka Infeksi Otak

content.text: Key clinical indicators suggesting brain infection include fever (not always high; may be low-grade in bacterial/TB or sudden high in viral), acute or subacute-chronic onset, clear focal neurological deficits, progressive drowsiness or altered mental status indicating decreasing consciousness, headache, and vomiting suggesting increased intracranial pressure.
Demam (bacterial/TB: tidak tinggi; viral: mendadak tinggi)
Onset: akut (viral, bacterial), subakut-kronis (TB, abses)
Defisit fokal yang jelas
Makin mengantuk/meracau (kesadaran menurun)
Nyeri kepala, muntah (tekanan intrakranial meningkat)
Fever pattern and onset timing provide important diagnostic clues

sections.title: Tersangka Infeksi SSP - HIV Stratification

content.text: The differential diagnosis for suspected brain infection must be stratified by HIV status and presence of focal neurological deficits.
In HIV+ with focal deficits: think toxoplasmosis first; without focal deficits: think cryptococcal or TB meningitis

sections.title: Lumbal Pungsi dan Karakteristik LCS

content.text: Lumbar puncture is the primary diagnostic procedure for CNS infection diagnosis. Key considerations include indications (therapeutic for cryptococcal meningitis intrathecal therapy; diagnostic for suspected CNS infection and neuroimmunological conditions like MS, NMO, GBS), and contraindications (absolute: impending brain herniation; relative: thrombocytopenia <50,000, local infection at puncture site, spinal cord mass).
Never perform LP if brain herniation is imminent - this is an absolute contraindication

sections.title: Toksoplasma Ensefalitis

content.text: Toxoplasma encephalitis is the most common opportunistic CNS infection in immunocompromised patients in Indonesia. It results from reactivation of latent Toxoplasma gondii infection. Diagnosis is predominantly presumptive based on clinical probability and response to empirical therapy. Definitive diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and pathology. PCR for Toxoplasma in CSF has low sensitivity (~50%) and is not recommended as routine.
Evaluasi ulang klinis dan radiologis setelah 2 minggu
Pyrimethamine + clindamycin is first-line; folinic acid protects against bone marrow suppression

sections.title: Meningitis Tuberkulosis

content.text: TB meningitis is difficult to diagnose because clinical symptoms are non-specific, BTA count in CSF is very low, and molecular diagnostics are not yet standard. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion in any patient with subacute fever, headache, and neurological symptoms.

The Thwaites score (Lancet 2002) helps differentiate bacterial from TB meningitis: Age >36 years (score 2), CSF WBC <900 cells/mm3 (score 3), peripheral WBC <15,000 (score 4), CSF neutrophils <75% (score 4), symptom duration >6 days (score -5). Total score >4 suggests bacterial meningitis; score <4 suggests TB meningitis.
MRC Grading: Grade I - fully conscious, no focal deficits; Grade IIa - GCS 15 with focal deficit; Grade IIb - GCS 10-14 with/without focal deficit; Grade III - GCS <10 with/without focal deficit.

Treatment: OAT for 9-12 months. First two weeks are 'life-saving.' Dexamethasone 0.4 mg/kg/day for 6-8 weeks is beneficial for HIV-negative patients (per meta-analysis). Vitamin B6 3x10mg po protects against OAT neurotoxicity. All patients with hydrocephalus or brain-spinal tuberculoma should be considered for surgical intervention.
Diagnosis definitif: PCR TB, GeneXpert, MGIT, BTA LCS positif
Diagnosis probabel: sel LCS >5 DAN Glucose ratio <0.5
B6 3x10mg po untuk melindungi dari neurotoksisitas OAT
Deksametason: 0.4 mg/kgBB/hr untuk 6-8 minggu
Thwaites GE et al. Lancet 2002;360:1287-92. Dexamethasone for TB meningitis. NEJM 2004;351(17):1741-51.
Penetration order: Pyrazinamid > Isoniazid > Rifampisin > Ethambutol > Streptomisin

sections.title: Meningitis Kriptokokus

content.text: Cryptococcal meningitis is generally opportunistic. Clinical presentation is subacute over 2-4 weeks with fever, headache, and high intracranial pressure. The presentation is often subtle with not all symptoms appearing as textbook descriptions. CT/MRI head typically shows no focal lesions.

Diagnosis options include: (1) Routine CSF analysis with India ink staining (rapid and inexpensive); (2) CSF and blood culture; (3) Blood serology; (4) Specimens from other sites such as skin lesions.

Acute phase therapy (Weeks 1-2): Amphotericin B 0.7-1 mg/kg per day IV drip over 4-6 hours in 250-500 ml D5% + Fluconazole 800 mg per day orally. Weeks 3-10: Fluconazole 800 mg/day orally. If amphotericin B is unavailable, fluconazole alone 800-2000 mg/day for 12 weeks. Maintenance phase: Fluconazole 200 mg/day until CD4 >200.
India ink is a rapid, cheap diagnostic tool; amphotericin B requires slow IV infusion in D5%

sections.title: Abses Serebri

content.text: Brain abscess clinically resembles other intracranial space-occupying lesions. The evolution progresses through four stages. Early cerebritis (days 1-3): hypodense area with surrounding partial contrast enhancement. Late cerebritis (days 4-9): ring enhancement around the hypodense center becoming more complete. Early capsule formation (days 10-13): necrotic center shrinks, capsule thickens. Late capsule formation (after day 14): capsule becomes increasingly well-defined and thick.

Once an abscess has formed, surgical excision or drainage combined with prolonged antibiotics (usually 4-8 weeks) remains the treatment of choice. Definitive therapy targets the cultured organism from biopsy or primary infection focus.
Early cerebritis: hari 1-3
Late cerebritis: hari 4-9
Early capsule formation: hari 10-13
Late capsule formation: setelah hari 14
Surgical indication: diameter >2.5cm, significant mass effect, ventricular proximity, or neurological deterioration

sections.title: Meningitis Bakterialis dan Ensefalitis Viral

content.text: Bacterial meningitis presents with the classic triad: fever, neck stiffness, and altered consciousness. Empirical antibiotic therapy should be broad-spectrum and initiated immediately after microbiological sampling. Definitive therapy is guided by culture results showing the identified organism and its antibiotic sensitivity/resistance patterns.

Viral encephalitis requires differentiated management based on immune status. In immunocompromised patients, look for CMV retinitis and perform LP PCR for HSV and VZV. In immunocompetent patients, perform LP PCR for CMV and examine skin/genital lesions. HSV typically involves the temporal lobes (limbic system); VZV affects the basal ganglia.
Trias meningitis: demam, kaku kuduk, penurunan kesadaran
Terapi empiris: antibiotik broad-spectrum dimulai sambil menunggu diagnosis pasti
Terapi definitif menunggu hasil kultur LCS

sections.title: Prinsip Penatalaksanaan Infeksi SSP

content.text: The general management of CNS infections follows a structured approach: (1) Handle emergencies including increased ICP with antiedema therapy, vital signs management with antipyretics and oxygenation, and metabolic correction via NGT; (2) Identify the causative microorganism through empirical clinical diagnosis and definitive testing including CSF analysis, neuroimaging, and other supportive investigations.
Menangani kegawatan: peningkatan TIK -> antiedema, tanda-tanda vital -> antipiretik, oksigenasi
Mencari mikroorganisme etiologi: empiris dari klinis, definitif dari pemeriksaan cairan otak, neuro-imaging, penunjang lain

diagnostic_logic.title: Localize the infection
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Determine if infection is in brain parenchyma, meninges, spinal cord, or extra-axial spaces

diagnostic_logic.title: Assess HIV status
diagnostic_logic.explanation: HIV status dramatically changes the differential diagnosis

diagnostic_logic.title: Identify focal vs diffuse pattern
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Focal deficits suggest toxoplasmosis, TB, or abscess; diffuse suggests meningitis or encephalitis

diagnostic_logic.title: Perform LP and neuroimaging
diagnostic_logic.explanation: CSF analysis and CT/MRI provide definitive diagnostic information

diagnostic_logic.title: Apply specific treatment protocols
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Each pathogen has specific antimicrobial regimen and duration

differential_notes.how_to_separate: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in immunocompromised; empirical trial of therapy confirms diagnosis
Subacute course, Thwaites score <4, basal meningeal enhancement, requires prolonged OAT
High ICP, India ink positive, subacute in immunocompromised
Focal lesion with capsule, four evolutionary stages on imaging

treatment_notes.content: Pyrimethamine 200mg loading then 25-75mg/day + clindamycin 2400mg/day for 3-6 weeks
OAT 9-12 months + dexamethasone 0.4mg/kg/day for 6-8 weeks + B6 protection
Amphotericin B 0.7-1mg/kg + fluconazole 800mg for 2 weeks, then fluconazole 800mg for 8 weeks, then 200mg maintenance until CD4 >200
Surgical drainage if >2.5cm or mass effect + 4-8 weeks antibiotics

red_flags: Imminent brain herniation (absolute contraindication to LP)
GCS <10 in TB meningitis (MRC Grade III - poor prognosis)
Abscess near ventricle or enlarging despite therapy
Cryptococcal meningitis with very high ICP
